plain.text: When Abram was ninety-nine, the LORD appeared to him: "I am God Almighty. Walk before me and be blameless. I will confirm my covenant with you and greatly multiply your descendants." Abram fell face down. God said, "You will be the father of many nations. No longer will you be called Abram; your name will be Abraham, for I have made you a father of many nations." Kings would come from him. God would be his God and the God of his descendants, and give them the whole land of Canaan as an everlasting possession.

God told Abraham that every male among them must be circumcised as the sign of the covenant, including boys at eight days old and those born in or bought into the household. God also said Sarai would be called Sarah, and he would bless her and give Abraham a son by her; she would be the mother of nations. Abraham fell face down and laughed, thinking, "Will a son be born to a man who is a hundred years old? Will Sarah bear a child at ninety?" He asked that Ishmael might live under God's blessing. God said, "Your wife Sarah will bear you a son, and you will name him Isaac ("he laughs"). I will establish my covenant with him." God would also bless Ishmael and make him into a great nation. That very day Abraham circumcised Ishmael and every male in his household, as God told him.

summary.bigIdea: God renews his covenant, gives Abram and Sarai new names, and promises them a son, Isaac.
points: Abram becomes Abraham, "father of many nations", and Sarai becomes Sarah.
Circumcision is given as the sign of the covenant.
Abraham laughs at the idea of a son in old age, but God promises Isaac.
summary.reflection: God gave Abraham and Sarah new names to match his promise. What do you think God's promise says about who you are?
